newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Down on late day swaps sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Down on late day swaps sell-off.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil ended weaker on Friday as the swaps market came under strong selling pressure late in the day in the absence of any physical activity, traders said.

Traders said the swaps was sold down in the evening as physical players shited their focus to the swaps market on talks of tight prompt cargoes which is deterring players from offering physical cargoes.
September swaps traded down to $104.00 per tonne from a traded high of $105.25 on Thursday. It was last quoted at $103.50/$104.00, down a dollar from Thursday.
Traders said unless fresh physical demand emerged next week, fuel oil trading was expected to be rangebound at the current higher level.
Fuel oil prices have risen by about $5.00 per tonne since the start of this month due to tight supplies and improved bunker sales.
The firmer prices were seen in the latest Chinese Petroleum Corp award for its fuel oil tender.
CPC sold by tender two 30,000-tonne cargoes of 3.0-percent sulphur, 180-centistoke fuel oil at just under $104 per tonne, traders said.
The award is $4.00 per tonne more than its previous award for an August 4-8 lifting cargo.
The cargoes were awarded to a Dutch trader and a Singapore trader, they said. The cargo is for September 11-20 lifting on a free-on-board Kaoshiung basis.
Similar higher prices was also seen in Sri Lanka's tender to sell fuel oil, reflecting a generally tight market.
British Petroleum made the highest bid into the tender to sell 19,000 tonnes of fuel oil.
The bid at $9.50 per tonne below Singapore spot quotes, on a free-on-board Colombo basis, is for Ceylon Petroleum Corp's revised tender for August 30-September 1 lifting dates.
In its previously awarded tender, CPC sold 20,000 tonnes of 3.5 percent sulphur fuel oil at a discount of $14.75 per tonne to Singapore spot quotes on an fob Colombo basis, for July 22-23 lifting.
